Section 14: Individual Vacation Days (IVDs) (7 I. & 23 I. 11.)
IVDs are a total of four to eight vacation days from a future vacation period (i.e., a vacation period that has
not had the PBS bid package for that bid period published in iCrew) that can be used all together or split into
two to four separate IVD periods each vacation year. A pilot with fewer than three weeks of earned vacation
may use up to four IVDs per vacation year on two separate occasions. A pilot with three or more weeks of
earned vacation may use up to six IVDs per vacation year, also on two separate occasions.
A pilot may be eligible for up to two additional IVDs and up to two additional separate occasions each
vacation year under Section 14 K.
The rules related to awarding of IVDs are identical to those for APDs but will be awarded prior to APDs. An
IVD(s) must be the first and/or last day(s) of an awarded vacation period. If a pilot uses an IVD(s) to drop a
trip(s) or on-call day(s), they will receive vacation pay for each IVD, regardless of the value of the rotation(s) or
reserve on call day(s) dropped.
For example, assume that a pilot has a 4-day rotation reporting July 10. So long as the reserves available
number for each day of the rotation is at least 25 percent of the number of reserves required, they may use
an IVD(s) to drop the rotation. They may use anywhere from one to four of their IVDs to drop the rotation,
which will drop with no pay. They will then be paid 4:35 for each IVD used.

day on which you have been awarded an IVD becomes a hard non-fly day on which you can neither be
awarded nor assigned flying. As with an APD, the Company may deny an IVD request regardless of the
number of reserves available during the period commencing two days before and ending one day after APD
holidays. For a list of those holidays, please see Section 23 I. 10.

flyback and paid per Section 14 E. 2. b.

rotation guarantee of 36:00 (the value of the original NOOP rotation).

original NOOP rotation 3305, Delta will debit the pilot's sick bank for 36:00.

for which the pilot is eligible is the difference between the value of rotation 0125 (36:00) and the value
